questions.question: Triacylglycerolsare composed of a). Three glycerol molecules and one fatty acid b). One glycerol molecule and three fatty acids c). One fatty acid and three glycerol molecules d). Two glycerol molecules and two fatty acids
questions.solution_html:
• Steps of Beta-Oxidation Cycle:
  • a. Oxidation: Acyl-CoA is oxidized by acyl-CoA dehydrogenase to form trans-enoyl-
  • CoA, producing FADH .₂. (2Mark)
  • b. Hydration: Enoyl-CoA hydratase adds water to form β-hydroxyacyl-CoA.
  • c. Oxidation: β-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase oxidizes it to β-ketoacyl-CoA,
  • producing NADH.
  • d. Cleavage: Thiolase splits β-ketoacyl-CoA to release acetyl-CoA and a shortened acyl-
  • CoA.

questions.question: Define β-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids and list the additional enzymes required.
questions.solution_html:
• Define B-oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids and list the additional enzymes required.
  • / (CO3)
  • ● Normal β-oxidation continues until a double bond is reached. (1Mark)
  • ● Enoyl-CoA isomerase converts the cis-Δ³ bond to trans-Δ², allowing oxidation to
  • proceed. (2Mark)
  • ● When multiple double bonds occur, 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase and enoyl-CoA
  • isomerase work together to form a usable intermediate. (2Mark)
  • ● After these modifications, β-oxidation resumes normally to produce energy.

questions.question: Describe how adipose tissue metabolism contributes to obesity.
questions.solution_html:
• Describe how adipose tissue metabolism contributes to obesity. / (CO3)
  • ● Excess calorie intake causes adipose tissue to store unlimited fat, leading to obesity
  • and insulin resistance. (1Mark)
  • ● Overloaded fat cells (adipocytes) get damaged, releasing triacylglycerol into the
  • extracellular space. (2Mark)
  • ● This leaked fat becomes non-functional “dead bulk”, adding weight without any
  • metabolic role. (2 Mark)

questions.question: Discuss the role of cholesterol catabolism in the formation of bile acids and bile salts.
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of cholesterol catabolism in the formation of bile acids and bile salts.
  • / (CO3)
  • ● Bile acids are the main end products of cholesterol breakdown in the liver and help
  • remove cholesterol. (2Mark)
  • ● The enzyme 7α-hydroxylase starts the process, forming cholic acid and
  • chenodeoxycholic acid (primary bile acids). (2Mark)
  • ● These acids join with glycine or taurine to form bile salts that help digest fats. (2Mark)
  • ● Bile salts are reused through enterohepatic circulation after being reabsorbed from the
  • intestine. (2Mark)
  • ● Lack of bile salts can cause gallstones, and chenodeoxycholic acid may be used to
  • dissolve them. (2Mark)
